turn_text: The W.D.E.L. News Time 446 says Delaware's afternoon news continues. Chris Carl joining you. Thanks for joining us here on W.D.E.L. And joining us now on the W.D.E.L. Newsline is Delaware Governor John Carney. Governor Carney, thanks for your time this afternoon.
Great to be with you, Chris. Thank you for your opportunity.
Our pleasure. Now we were told today that the state is setting up a new statewide testing plan that goes into effect on Monday. Why don't you give us a sense of what is being laid out for next week?

Yeah, so all the testing that's been done across the state of Delaware and it hasn't been enough over the last several weeks as the virus has been spread has been done with the state public health lab and at the individual hospitals. It became clear, number one, that we needed more tests than we started to get those from the private sector and from the federal government and that we needed to do this to have a testing plan that was coordinated and statewide. And so we're standing on that kind of as we speak, the hospitals are taking the lead. It will require someone to go to their primary care physician or if they don't have a primary care physician to call the hotline and get a referral to go to two testing sites. The Christiana care is standing up, one at the Wilmington campus and one down at Churchman's Crossing. A testing site that they help is standing up at their two sites that BB is standing up in Eastern Sussex there and then a testing site at Nanoco Hospital in Western Sussex County. So we have the availability to do more testing. It really is still for people who are symptomatic, who have flu-like symptoms, have a cough and a respiratory distress and a fever, and so they get some kind of screening. It'll be an easy screen. One that you can do over the telephone. We don't want folks to go to the emergency room. If you go to the emergency room, if they are a Christian of care, they'll triage you through a tent that they've set out outside and try to keep you out of the emergency room so you're not impacting others. And so this is going to be a big step forward. We'll be able to test more people, let them know where they stand and have a better idea of the infection. as it is of being transmitted through our state.

turn_text: And just to be clear, it's not open testing for anyone per se. There is a process to go through which starts with contacting your doctor, correct?

That's exactly right. And to be clear, you know, it doesn't matter. It's a very symptomatic, meaning you don't have these really like symptoms. The test I'm told from their physician, the test doesn't work anyway. And so you really do have to be symptomatic. But we haven't been testing all of the people that have been symptomatic, you know, if you're younger and not at great risk, we've just told folks to stay at home and to self-isolate, self-quarantines for 12, 14 days. But now we'll be able to test many more people to give them an idea of whether they have just the flu or whether they have just the hay fever that's coming on now in the spring or actually have the virus. And that means we're going to have more positive cases And we'll react with respect to public restrictions based on what we see across our state.
What is your feeling at this point, Delaware is standing at just 38. But as you said, that will likely go up with more testing. But how do you feel about where we are right now?

Well, the thing that worries me the most is people just aren't paying attention to our advice to stay out of crowded public places. I was just at the beach to take a look at that. The beaches were full of folks. We might have to close the beaches, you know, people are just congregating in large gatherings. And, you know, we had originally said the gatherings of 100 or more needed to be canceled. People didn't pay attention to that last weekend as they celebrated and beat up the St. Patty's Day. We had to close the bars in restaurants so that it was over that. And we've ratcheted that down to gatherings of 50 or more. We might have to take that down further and even recommend closing businesses that are open. We'll always obviously keep essential businesses that are open and those businesses that are open and people in general need to follow the advice. Make sure that they're sanitizing their hand, that they're wiping down surfaces that are touched a lot, that they're covering their car, if they're sick, that they're isolating at home and staying at home. Because if we do that, we'll be able to reduce the spread here at the front end so we don't get too many cases which in the back end will overload our hospital system and we don't want that to happen.

Yeah we certainly could get to that point if people don't pay attention to you know voluntary restrictions and restrictions where we ordering people but they're just not following those orders. New York has a much worse situation on the ground. We don't want to have that situation. We're going to be as cautious as possible, recognizing that everything you do has an effect on people's livelihoods mostly in terms of the shut off of economic activity and jobs.
And finally, we hear a lot from parents who are just trying to figure out what to do next. What's the prognosis for schools at this point?

Yeah, well, so we directed them to be closed for two weeks. We're going to look at that over the weekend. I think it's likely that we're going to have to extend that. I still want to see the reports back from the districts in terms of what they're doing to try to get some instruction going on remotely, getting the younger children to be reading, getting reading material into their hands, and advising parents and caregivers to do that. Feeding the children the districts have done a really good job. grab and go kinds of lunches and breakfast as we feed a lot of children in the schools and the districts and schools are doing a very good job there. But we're going to evaluate that situation over the weekend and try to come up with a decision in the middle of the week, Thursday at the latest to provide some advice there. It's likely that we'll have to extend that shutdown. Alright,
